key.name: show-workspace-indicator
key.description: Show workspace indicator in the top panel displaying workspace numbers for each monitor

key.name: flat-panel-indicator
key.summary: Flatten the panel indicator into a single row
key.description: Show all monitors in one horizontal row, ordered left to right. When disabled the indicator is grouped into rows by vertical position, which stacks monitors on different heights - for example a portrait monitor next to landscape ones - into several panel rows

key.name: warp-pointer-to-focus
key.description: When focus changes via keyboard (Alt+Tab, dock, etc.), move pointer to the center of the newly focused window

key.name: focus-follows-mouse
key.description: When enabled, hovering a window focuses it, without having to click. Switches Mutter's own focus-mode between 'sloppy' and 'click'; the previous value is restored when the extension is disabled

key.name: saved-focus-mode
key.description: Internal: the org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences focus-mode value that was active before this extension changed it, so it can be restored on disable

key.name: raise-on-cycle-focus
key.description: When cycling focus between windows, also raise the window to the top of the stack

key.name: workspace-modifier
key.description: Modifier key used for workspace switching (Mod+1-0) and window moving (Mod+Shift+1-0)

key.name: workspace-switch-mode
key.description: When switching to a workspace already shown on another monitor: 'swap' exchanges workspaces between monitors, 'warp' moves pointer to that monitor instead

key.name: monitor-workspace-map
key.summary: Workspace shown on each monitor at startup
key.description: JSON array of {"monitor":N,"workspace":N} entries defining which workspace each monitor displays after login. An empty list means automatic: the primary monitor keeps the workspace that is currently active and every other monitor gets the next free one. Workspaces are zero-based indices as used everywhere else, so workspace 1 in the UI is index 0

key.name: app-workspace-map
key.description: JSON array of {"wmClass":"NAME","workspace":N,"scope":"startup|always","maximize":BOOL} entries. A window whose WM_CLASS matches is moved to that workspace without ever activating it, so the view never jumps, and maximized right after the move when the rule says so. scope 'startup' only applies within the first 30 seconds after login, which covers autostarted apps and nothing else; scope 'always' applies every time the app opens. 'maximize' is optional and falls back to the maximize-app-windows default. Workspaces are zero-based indices, so workspace 1 in the UI is index 0. An empty list disables the feature

key.name: maximize-app-windows
key.summary: Default for new application rules: open maximized
key.description: Whether a newly added app-workspace-map rule gets 'maximize' set. A rule without its own 'maximize' field follows this value, a rule that sets it ignores this value. Windows are only ever maximized, never restored
